items.title: Maps between modules over a flat covering that are I-power torsion in kernel and cokernel come from maps over the base ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and establishes two dual statements: given an R-module N and an S-module map M' -> N tensor_R S whose kernel and cokernel are I-power torsion, there is an R-module map M -> N and an isomorphism M tensor_R S = M' compatible with these; and symmetrically for a map out of M tensor_R S (source lines 24881-24899). The proof is a genuine application of the gluing equivalence rather than a citation of the conclusion. It writes I = (f_1, ..., f_t) and observes that the localizations at the f_i of the given map are isomorphisms, so that (M', N_{f_i}, varphi_{f_i}, can_{ij}) is an object of the gluing category (proof lines 24902-24906). The equivalence proposition then produces an R-module M with M' = M tensor_R S and N_{f_i} = M_{f_i} compatibly (proof lines 24907-24910). The remaining content is the functoriality step: the displayed morphism in the gluing category whose first component is varphi corresponds to an R-module map psi : M -> N under the equivalence of categories, and the composition of the base change of psi with the isomorphism M' = M tensor_R S is varphi, which is exactly the compatibility (proof lines 24911-24924). Part (2) is carried out as the dual argument with varphi_{f_i}^{-1} replacing varphi_{f_i} (proof lines 24927-24948), and the final kernel-and-cokernel statement is drawn from the neighbourhood equivalence lemma (proof lines 24951-24952). The non-routine content is the translation of a map of glued objects back to a map over R.
